about: P4-K05 retrieval benchmark for the context compiler. A workspace knowledge pack of 17 multi-section documents with links (ITSM and sales), and 32 hand-labelled questions written before any configuration was run (2026-09-25). `expected` is the section the answer is in (path#anchor); `type` is direct (shares words with the section), paraphrase (avoids them), section (the answer is not in the document's first section) or hop (the question names a document that LINKS to the answer's document). Not a held-out set in the statistical sense: small, written by the implementer.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: An incident breaches its service level agreement when it is not resolved within the target time for its priority; made_sla is false.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.text: Time spent in a waiting state for the requester is paused and not counted. Incidents cancelled by the requester are excluded from the breach rate.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.text: P1 must be resolved in 4 hours, P2 in 8 hours, P3 in 3 business days and P4 in 10 business days.

sections.heading: Calendar
sections.text: P3 and P4 targets count business hours only, Monday to Friday 8:00 to 18:00 local time; public holidays are excluded.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: States in which the resolution clock stops: awaiting customer, awaiting vendor and scheduled change window.

sections.heading: Audit
sections.text: Pauses longer than 5 days need a manager approval note on the record.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: An incident moved back from resolved to in progress within 7 days of resolution because the fix did not hold.

sections.heading: Counting
sections.text: A reopen counts against the quality of the original fix; the reopened incident keeps its original number.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: Share of resolved incidents that were never reopened.

sections.heading: Calculation
sections.text: Count of resolved incidents with reopen_count equal to zero divided by all resolved incidents in the period.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: A P1 incident affecting more than one business service or more than 100 users, declared by the duty manager.

sections.heading: Communication
sections.text: Status updates go to stakeholders every 30 minutes until service is restored.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.text: Every declared outage of that class gets a blameless review with root cause, contributing factors and follow-up actions owned by the problem manager.

sections.heading: Deadline
sections.text: The review document is due five working days after restoration.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: Open incidents older than their priority target at the end of a day.

sections.heading: Ageing buckets
sections.text: Reported in three bands: 0 to 7 days, 8 to 30 days, and over 30 days.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: Average elapsed hours from incident opened to service restored, excluding paused time.

sections.heading: Caveat
sections.text: Skewed by a few very long incidents; report the median alongside the mean.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: A subscription customer who did not renew within 30 days after the contract end date.

sections.heading: Voluntary vs involuntary
sections.text: Involuntary churn is a failed payment; voluntary churn is an explicit cancellation by the customer.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: Recurring revenue this month from accounts that existed twelve months ago, divided by their recurring revenue twelve months ago, including expansion, contraction and lost accounts.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: A signed order, recorded when the contract is countersigned and before invoicing.

sections.heading: Recognition
sections.text: Revenue from a booking is recognised over the service period, not at signature.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.text: Discounts above 20 percent need the regional sales director; above 35 percent they need the CFO.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: Open opportunities in the stages from qualify to negotiate, each weighted by its stage probability.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.text: Qualify 10 percent, develop 25 percent, propose 50 percent, negotiate 75 percent.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.text: A period when only emergency changes may be deployed, for example the last two weeks of the fiscal year.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.text: Normal changes need approval at the weekly meeting; standard pre-approved changes do not.
